title: Run Better AI Coding Agents for $0 — Straight From Your Own Laptop
description:
Looking for a chill but productive space to code, learn, and connect with other developers? Whether you’re just starting out or deep into a side project, you’re welcome here.

🚨 **Special Feature This Week: Local Coding Agents** This week features a hands-on walkthrough by **[Eugene Oskin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eugene-oskin/)**, who will be showing us how to set up local LLMs on a MacBook to run coding agents that hit Sonnet 4.5 levels of performance.
He’ll be breaking down his exact stack:

* **The Software:** Configuring LM Studio (Developer mode) and setting up local REST API endpoints.
* **The Hardware:** Pushing an Apple M4 Max with 64GB RAM to dedicate over 51GB of VRAM for model acceleration.
* **The Models:** Live demos of loading and running **Qwen3.6-27b** alongside the highly efficient **Nvidia Nemotron models family**.

Alongside the demo, this remains a casual, community-driven space where you can:

* 💻 Work on your own coding projects
* 🎯 Share goals or progress (totally optional!)
* 🎙️ Talk tech and discuss local AI setups
* ☕ Meet like-minded people over coffee

Come with your laptop, your curiosity, or just a love for tech. Stay for the connections and good vibes.
☕ *This event is hosted at a local café, so we kindly ask that you support the venue by purchasing a drink or snack if you can.*
No pressure, no strict schedule—just code, coffee, AI, and vibes.

Welcome to the next [AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group](https://www.meetup.com/aws-canberra-well-architected-user-group/) Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

* **Yadwinder Sharma, Founder, https://www.nimbal.ai**

**From 5 Days to 5 Minutes: Reimagining Well-Architected QA with Autonomous AI**

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more

In this talk we will go into the detail of not only the launch of the first Well-Architected agents from both AWS and other AWS partners (and what they can and can't do) but will also go through best-practice agentic architecture as verified by AWS senior architects.

**AI Landing Zones**
As organisations rapidly adopt AI, many struggle to move beyond isolated proofs of concept into secure, scalable, and governed production environments. This session explores how AI Landing Zones provide the foundational platform needed to operationalise AI safely and sustainably at enterprise scale.

**Chanaka Nissanka** is a Principal Consultant based in Auckland, with extensive experience helping large enterprises design and adopt cloud platforms at scale. He specialises in Azure Landing Zones, cloud governance, and operating model design, working closely with architects, security teams, and business stakeholders to enable secure, scalable cloud and AI adoption. Chanaka has led and advised on complex transformation initiatives across regulated and high‑consumption environments, bridging strategy and hands‑on implementation.

title: Playfight
location: Silo Hall, 3 East Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Playfight by Julia Grogan
Under their tree, three 15 year-old girls - Keira, Zainab and Lucy - wrestle with sex, shame and growing up at different paces.
It starts with a game and a dead possum. It ends with someone getting hurt.
Fast, funny, and unfiltered Playfight hurls us into a world where boundaries blur and expectations collide. A viral video, awkward first times and friendship stretched to breaking point. These are the milestones of a coming-of-age story that’s as raw as it is dangerous.
Julia Grogan’s award-winning debut isn’t here to judge or offer easy answers. Instead, Playfight asks what happens when no one teaches you how to look after yourself and you have to figure it out with just your mates, your instincts and the internet.
An Edinburgh Festival smash hit, Playfight shines a vivid light on adolescent desire in a landscape of rising sexual violence.

title: Mozart
location: Auckland Town Hall, 301-317 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland
description:
Conductor Samy RachidViolin James Ehnes
Mozart Symphony No.35 ‘Haffner’Mozart Violin Concerto No.4Chausson Symphony in B-flat
It’s always a huge pleasure to welcome back to Auckland the superlative violinist James Ehnes, joining us with Mozart’s sparkling concerto.
This is preceded by another piece of Mozartian effervescence, which its composer said should be played ‘very fiery’ and ‘as fast as possible’.
Then one of the finest symphonies in the French tradition. Chausson’s only excursion into the form covers a dramatic range of emotions, from its exuberant first movement to its entreating close.

title: The Queen's Nanny
location: The PumpHouse Theatre, Killarney Park, 2a Manurere Avenue, Takapuna, Auckland 0622, Auckland
description:
Marion Crawford, affectionately known as “Crawfie”, spent sixteen years as nanny to the young princesses Elizabeth and Margaret.
Melanie Tait has constructed a superbly written, witty, insightful and poignant play examining the power, sacrifice, hurt and betrayal of a time in history when loyalty was demanded, the barriers of class were strictly defined, and the right to tell one’s own story was non-existent.
Director Simon Prast steers this personal drama, a commentary on class and the monarchy, into an unmissable night of theatre, with an exceptional cast.
Anna Jullienne plays Crawfie, balancing humour and heartbreak as her loyalty is questioned.
Laura Hill is the Queen Mother, expertly defining the machinations of the House of Windsor, both funny and at times faintly ridiculous.
The third cast member is Jack Buchanan, who has the task of portraying seven characters throughout the play, led by the narrator, steering the action almost as a ringmaster. He also manages to become a butler, an American editor, Crawfie’s fiancée and even a young Elizabeth!
Needless to say, another Tadpole masterpiece not to be missed.
Runtime: Approx. 2 hours with an intervalAge Recommendation: All ages

description:
Wriggle and Rhyme is a programme that promotes active movement and brain development for babies and toddlers aged two years and under.
Join us for a free fun session that uses resources and music to support the development of your baby or toddler. Our enthusiastic team offer an inclusive session for you and your precious pēpē.

title: The Lamplighters
location: Howick Little Theatre, 1 Sir Lloyd Drive, Pakuranga, Auckland 2010, Auckland
description:
By the creator and writer of Taggart comes The Lamplighters:
In a remote Cumbrian farmhouse, three former detectives reunite on the anniversary of a murder case that still haunts them. When they are joined by a determined young crime writer who is unwilling to let the past lie, old loyalties splinter and buried secrets start to surface. As mist closes in and the night deepens, their friendship falters and after 10 years the truth may finally emerge.
Recommended for ages 16+. Contains strong language and adult themes.

title: Movement therapy for mamas and bubbas
location: Freemans Bay Community Centre, 52 Hepburn Street, Freemans Bay, Auckland, Auckland
description:
We are thrilled to have Rewa Fowles facilitating these sessions. Through ‘Movement Therapy for Mamas and Bubbas’ Rewa desires to cultivate a space where mamas and their children are welcome to unapologetically be themselves through creative movement.
A time to release stress, be playful, and create connections!
Mamas you’re invited to bring your young children to these sessions, where you will learn how to regulate your bodies by not controlling it - but by getting more familiar and in tune with what your body needs.
Parking is available on-site and via Pratt Street (rear entrance).
